children: Nscale, a vertically integrated AI infrastructure and cloud platform, filed a Form S-1 to go public on the NYSE under the symbol "NSCL." The UK‑based company plans to use proceeds to fund data center projects and deployments, technology development, working capital, and possible acquisitions. There has been no prior public market for its shares.

Nscale is a full‑stack AI hyperscaler that combines low‑cost power, purpose‑built data centers, and large‑scale GPU clusters with a unified software control plane. The company operates two primary products: Nscale Infrastructure, which delivers dedicated, high‑performance AI compute under long‑term take‑or‑pay contracts, and Nscale Cloud, which provides managed platform and AI services for inference, fine‑tuning, and orchestration. Its vertically integrated approach spans powered land acquisition, behind‑the‑meter generation, modular liquid‑cooled data centers, fleet operations software, and enterprise‑grade cloud services. Nscale has announced a definitive agreement to acquire Anyscale, the commercial platform behind Ray, to enhance its platform layer and deepen its open‑source‑led adoption strategy.

The company serves hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, AI‑native developers, enterprises, and sovereign customers. It emphasizes cost efficiency via renewable‑rich, low‑cost power regions and modular, repeatable buildouts to accelerate time‑to‑power. Contracts are predominantly multi‑year, take‑or‑pay agreements designed to provide revenue visibility and support capital deployment across its campus and distributed footprints.
: AI infrastructure is undergoing the “largest build‑out in history,” driven by adoption of training and inference at scale.
: Demand for high‑density, GPU‑optimized data centers is outpacing supply and expected to continue rising.
: Nscale pursues a power‑first, vertically integrated model with line of sight to approximately 10 GW of potential power capacity.
: CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe, Lambda; hyperscalers including AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle; and emerging large‑scale compute providers such as SpaceX.
: Shift to Tier‑2/Tier‑3 markets, behind‑the‑meter power, liquid cooling, open‑source distributed compute (Ray), and growing sovereign AI requirements.
: Long‑term agreements with leading technology companies; signed statements of work with Microsoft (up to ~$43.8B) and Anthropic (up to ~$44.6B) subject to delivery and financing conditions.
: Five active and twelve contracted data center sites (seven wholly‑owned, nine colocation, one leased) as of August 31, 2026.
: Operations concentrated in renewable‑rich, low‑cost power regions including Norway, Portugal, Iceland, select U.S. locations, and APAC; platform operates in 14 regions.
: Announced acquisition of Anyscale (Ray); strategic collaboration with Microsoft; preferred infrastructure provider to Figure AI under a multi‑year GPU services agreement.
: Approximately $2.6B active and $103.4B active and contracted total contract value (TCV) as of August 31, 2026; weighted average contract life ~5.7 years.

: ~25,000 active GPUs and ~461,000 active and contracted GPUs; ~1.37 GW of active and contracted capacity; line of sight to ~10 GW potential power capacity; billions of tokens processed on Nscale Cloud; team of 1,000+ employees.
: Up 1,252% vs. $10.4 million in the prior‑year period
, Founder and Chief Executive Officer - Founded Nscale after leading Arkon Energy; experience in digital infrastructure, venture formation, and capital markets.
, Chief Financial Officer - Over two decades at J.P. Morgan; former Managing Director in Equity Capital Markets covering Tech, Media & Telecom.
, Chief Business Officer and President, EMEA - Former banker at JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and Standard Chartered; leads European rollout and sovereign AI initiatives.
, President, APAC - Former VP at Alibaba Cloud; senior roles at Ant Group and Lazada; prior AWS infrastructure leadership.
, President, AI Infrastructure - Former Corporate VP for Azure AI, led development/deployment of AI infrastructure and hyperscale supercomputers.
, President, Data Centers - Former SVP of Data Center Infrastructure at Oracle; senior roles at Vantage Data Centers.
, Chief Legal Officer - Former corporate counsel across financial services and infrastructure; leads global legal and governance.
: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC; J.P. Morgan; Morgan Stanley (lead bookrunners)
: General corporate purposes, including funding data center projects and deployments, technology development, working capital and operating expenses; potential acquisitions or investments.
